subject: history_social
notes: Razia Sultan ruled the Delhi Sultanate from 1236 to 1240.
She was the only woman ever to sit on the throne of the Delhi Sultanate.
Her father, Sultan Iltutmish, had reportedly named her as his successor in preference to her brothers.
Coins issued during her reign bore her own name and royal titles.
The chronicler Minhaj-i-Siraj, a contemporary, wrote that she gave up seclusion and appeared in public wearing a tunic and cap.
stem: The student wants to emphasize both that Razia's position was unique in the Delhi Sultanate and that she presented herself publicly as a ruler. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Reportedly named as successor by her father, Iltutmish, in preference to her brothers, Razia became the only woman to rule the Delhi Sultanate.
choices.B: Coins issued during Razia's reign (1236–1240) bore her own name and royal titles, and she appeared in public wearing a tunic and cap.
choices.C: The Delhi Sultanate's only woman ruler, Razia issued coins bearing her name and, a chronicler reports, appeared publicly in a tunic and cap.
choices.D: According to Minhaj-i-Siraj, Razia, who ruled the Delhi Sultanate from 1236 to 1240, gave up seclusion and appeared in public in a tunic and cap.

explanation.why: The goal has two parts. Her uniqueness comes from the note that she was the only woman ever to rule the Delhi Sultanate. Her public self-presentation as a ruler comes from the coins in her name and her appearing in public in a tunic and cap. The key must combine both.
explanation.A: Incorrect. This establishes that her position was unique, but it says nothing about how she presented herself in public.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This shows how she presented herself as a ruler, but it never says that her position was unique.
explanation.C: Correct. It opens with her uniqueness (the only woman ruler) and then gives two ways she presented herself publicly as a ruler.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This shows her public self-presentation and names the source, but like B, it leaves out that she was the only woman to hold the throne.
